question: Which minorities are mentioned in article 30 of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Linguistic and religious__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Minorities are granted the freedom to create and run their educational institutions. **Also known as the "Charter of Education Rights," Article 30.
 
• **Article 30(1)**
 
 
• All minorities must have the freedom to create and run the educational institutions of their choice, regardless of whether they are classified as religious or linguistic minorities.
 
• 1 (A):
 
 
• The State shall ensure that the **amount fixed by or determined under such law for the acquisition of any property** of an educational institution established and administered by a minority, as referenced in clause (1), is such as would not restrict or abrogate the right guaranteed under that clause.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Article 30(2)**
 
 
• The **state is prohibited from discriminating against any educational institution** on the grounds that it is run by a minority, regardless of their religion or language, while providing financial support to educational institutions.​​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Constitution went into effect on **January 26, 1950.** The Constitution was the longest national constitution ever approved at the time of its ratification.
 
• It had **395 Articles, 8 Schedules, and was about 145,000 words long.**
 
• During the course of 11 sessions and 167 days, spanning two years and eleven months, the members of the Constituent Assembly deliberated on every article of the Constitution.
 
• The **Articles are divided into 22 different portions**, which corresponds to how the **Constitution of India, 1950's** text has them arranged.
 
• The** Schedules to the Constitution, **which now** number 12,** give into more detail about government policy or regulations in respect to particular Constitutional Articles.
